[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Test Isolation in Ruby on Rails with FactoryBot and DatabaseCleaner"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"A reliable test suite is the backbone of any robust Ruby on Rails application. One of the most common pitfalls in testing is test pollution, where data created in one test leaks into another, causing flaky and unpredictable results. Achieving true test isolation requires a combination of FactoryBot for generating test data and DatabaseCleaner for resetting state between runs."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Test Isolation"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Test isolation ensures that every test runs in a clean, predictable environment. Regardless of the order in which your tests execute, they should neither depend on nor affect the state of the database left by previous tests. Without proper isolation, a failing test might pass when run in isolation, or passing tests might fail unexpectedly when the entire suite is executed."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Adding the Gems"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"To get started, add FactoryBot and DatabaseCleaner to your application's Gemfile inside the development and test groups."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"group :development, :test do
  gem 'factory_bot_rails'
  gem 'database_cleaner-active_record'
end"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Run 'bundle install' to install the gems."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Configuring DatabaseCleaner"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Rails uses database transactions by default to rollback changes after each test. However, when dealing with JavaScript-driven feature specs (like Capybara with Selenium), the test runs in a separate thread and database transactions will not see uncommitted data. DatabaseCleaner solves this by allowing strategy-based cleaning."},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create or update your configuration file at 'spec/support/database_cleaner.rb':"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"RSpec.configure do |config|
  config.before(:suite) do
    DatabaseCleaner.clean_with(:truncation)
  end

  config.before(:each) do
    DatabaseCleaner.strategy = :transaction
  end

  config.before(:each, js: true) do
    DatabaseCleaner.strategy = :truncation
  end

  config.before(:each) do
    DatabaseCleaner.start
  end

  config.after(:each) do
    DatabaseCleaner.clean
  end
end"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Defining Factories with FactoryBot"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"FactoryBot replaces traditional fixtures with a clean, programmatic approach to defining test data. Create a factory for a User model in 'spec/factories/users.rb':"},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"FactoryBot.define do
  factory :user do
    sequence(:email) { |n| "user#{n}@example.com" }
    name { "John Doe" }
    role { "member" }

    trait :admin do
      role { "admin" }
    end
  end
end"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Writing Isolated Tests"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"With DatabaseCleaner wiping the state and FactoryBot generating fresh data, your specs remain entirely isolated. Here is an example model spec:"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"require 'rails_helper'

RSpec.describe User, type: :model do
  it "is valid with valid attributes" do
    user = build(:user)
    expect(user).to be_valid
  end

  it "allows creating admin users using traits" do
    admin = create(:user, :admin)
    expect(admin.role).to eq("admin")
  end
end"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Clean Testing"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Prefer 'build' over 'create' when testing validations or methods that do not require database persistence to speed up your test suite."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use DatabaseCleaner transaction strategy for fast, memory-based rollbacks on standard specs, and truncation specifically for asynchronous feature specs."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid hardcoding primary keys or unique attributes like emails without using sequences to prevent validation collisions."}]
